expectations.text: All 5 Jonah Rhythm steps are present: Emma catalyzes, Emma exits, James struggles, James discovers, Emma returns
expectations.evidence: Emma catalyzes: shows the script and says 'Find it' (line 7-8). Emma exits: 'She picked up her notebook... The door clicked shut.' (line 11-14). James struggles: runs the script, compares output to spec, hand-calculates, adds print statement (lines 17-41). James discovers: identifies surcharge is 0.45 instead of 0.35 by working backward from expected output (lines 41-44). Emma returns: 'Emma came back, coffee in hand' (line 55), validates his find and teaches root cause tracing to source of truth (lines 55-79).

expectations.text: Emma's exit has a natural reason
expectations.evidence: 'I have a standup in fifteen minutes.' (line 8). A standup is a routine workplace meeting, a natural and specific reason to leave.

James does not know which output is wrong at first (line 19). He hand-calculates on scrap paper (line 29). He recalculates to confirm his own math (line 32). He adds a debug print statement to confirm his hypothesis (lines 35-39). The process is shown step by step over ~15 lines of prose, not compressed into a summary.

expectations.text: James makes a genuine partial discovery on his own
expectations.evidence: James identifies the bug fully (surcharge 0.45 should be 0.35, lines 41-44) and recognizes his gap: 'He had found what was wrong. He had not figured out why it was wrong.' (line 49). The discovery is genuine and arrived at through a demonstrated debugging process (compare spec to output, add print, work backward).

expectations.text: Emma's return validates James's discovery AND fills the remaining gap
expectations.evidence: Validates: 'Good process.' (line 63). Fills gap: Emma asks 'Where does the surcharge come from?' (line 71), guiding James to trace the hardcoded literal, then teaches the principle: 'constants like pricing belong in a single source of truth, not scattered across functions' (lines 75-76). She fills exactly the gap James identified (why it was wrong, not just what was wrong).

expectations.text: Emma occupies approximately 20-30% of the page time
expectations.evidence: The narrative is ~82 lines. Emma is present and speaking in lines 7-14 (opening, ~8 lines) and lines 55-81 (closing, ~27 lines), totaling ~35 lines. 35/82 = ~43%. However, much of the closing section is James speaking or thinking while Emma asks questions. Emma's direct speech and action is closer to 20-22 lines out of 82, which is ~25-27%. The rhythm is correct: James owns the middle solo section (~40 lines) which dominates the piece.

expectations.text: At least 1 monologue breaker is present
expectations.evidence: Line 29: 'He grabbed a scrap of paper from his desk, a habit from his operations days when reconciling supplier invoices.' This is a physical action that interrupts the internal reasoning monologue and connects to James's backstory. Also line 45: 'It felt like reconciling a purchase order against an invoice' is an extended analogy breaker.

expectations.text: James uses at least 1 voice marker
expectations.evidence: Multiple voice markers tying to James's operations/logistics background: 'a habit from his operations days when reconciling supplier invoices' (line 29); 'reconciling a purchase order against an invoice, finding the one line item where the supplier quoted a different unit price' (line 45); 'That was how his old company handled contract rates: one master sheet, every department pulled from it' (line 77). These are consistent character-specific references to his pre-coding career.

expectations.text: The emotional tone matches growing confidence for Chapter 15
expectations.evidence: Explicit confidence progression: 'Three weeks ago he would have stared at this for twenty minutes, then asked Emma. Today it took him four.' (line 47). He 'almost smiled' (line 47). The final line captures earned maturity: 'the lesson... about tracing a value to its source and asking why it was wrong, not just what was wrong, that was the part that would stick' (line 81). The tone is steady growth, not beginner panic or expert ease.

expectations.text: The debugging scenario involves a realistic Python error
expectations.evidence: The scenario is a shipping cost calculator where a per-kilo surcharge is hardcoded as 0.45 instead of the spec's 0.35, producing 12.50 instead of 11.50 for the medium tier. This is a realistic 'logic bug with no traceback' scenario: the code runs cleanly but produces wrong output due to a mismatched constant. The debugging process (compare output to spec, add print statements, trace backward) is standard Python debugging practice.

claims.claim: The narrative is 500-600 words as prompted
claims.evidence: Word count is approximately 590 words (excluding the HTML comment header), within the 500-600 word target.

claims.claim: Density is 65% as stated in the header comment
claims.evidence: The narrative is almost entirely technical content (debugging process, code snippets, debugging reasoning) woven through character interaction. Non-technical filler is minimal.

claims.claim: Patterns used include P2 Emma Fallibility (Type A)
claims.evidence: Line 67-68: Emma shares a personal failure: 'I once spent two hours fixing a billing bug. Changed the rate, shipped it, moved on. A week later the same bug came back because the rate was being pulled from a config file I never updated. I fixed the shadow, not the source.' This is a Type A fallibility moment (sharing a past mistake).

suggestions.assertion: Emma occupies approximately 20-30% of page time
suggestions.reason: This assertion is difficult to evaluate objectively. 'Page time' could mean lines of text, word count, or scenes where Emma is present. In this run, Emma is present in the opening and closing sections which together span ~43% of lines, but her direct dialogue and action is closer to 25%. The assertion should specify the measurement method (e.g., 'Emma's direct speech and actions comprise 20-30% of the total word count').

No assertion checks whether the code snippets shown are syntactically valid Python. This run includes print(f"DEBUG: base={base_rate}...") which is correct, but a run with broken syntax would still pass all assertions.

eval_feedback.overall: Strong eval set. The Jonah Rhythm steps are well-tested. The page-time assertion needs a clearer measurement definition. Consider adding an assertion for code correctness in snippets.
